title: Topic 11 · Status Games vs. Wealth Creation · Chunks
source: Modern Wisdom · Chris Williamson & Naval Ravikant · youtu.be/KyfUysrNaco

items.s: Satisfaction games, the allure of accruing, whether it’s fame, actual fame, or just the competition comparison trap, it’s always there.
Satisfaction games, the allure of accruing, whether it’s fame, actual fame, or just the competition comparison trap, it’s always there.
There’s a real draw of being swayed by social approval, but how should people learn to get less distracted by status games in that way?

items.c: there was no such thing as wealth
items.s: In old society, let’s go back to hunter-gatherer times, there was no such thing as wealth – you just had what you could carry.
You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.
It’s a ranking ladder, it’s a hierarchy, and so if one person rises in status, somebody else has to lower in status.
They’re always combative.
So I would argue that wealth creation games are both more pleasant, they’re positive-sum, and they actually have concrete material returns.

items.zh: 我们在进化上天生如此
items.s: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.

items.c: it's not gonna fall on your lap
items.zh: 它不会自己掉到你怀里
items.s: You still have to go find it, it’s not easy, it’s not gonna fall on your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting,

items.c: almost no way out of that
items.s: A few hundred years ago you were born a serf, you were gonna die a serf, there was almost no way out of that.
A lot of people do that, as you said.
That’s a good observation, I hadn’t thought that through, but you’re right.

items.c: trajectory is more important than position
items.s: Jimmy Carr has this cool idea where he says trajectory is more important than position.
Something that is bleeding eventually dies, unless you stop the bleeding, so you’re hardwired not to lose what you have.

items.c: don’t matter as much as they used to
items.note: not as ... as ... 比较现在与过去；used to 省略了 matter。 例：Status games don’t matter as much as they used to.
items.s: I think it just helps to see that status games don’t matter as much as they used to.

items.note: what 引出“你能够……的东西”，不是问句。 例：You only had what you could carry.
items.s: In old society, let’s go back to hunter-gatherer times, there was no such thing as wealth – you just had what you could carry.

items.zh: 当时仅有的那一点东西
items.note: what little 强调“少得可怜的数量”。 例：They shared what little was available.
items.s: If you were high status, then you got what little was available first, but even back then you had to earn your status by taking care of the tribe.

items.c: earn your status by taking care of the tribe
items.zh: 通过照顾部落来赢得地位
items.note: earn ... by doing ... 表示通过某种行动赢得某种结果。 例：You earn trust by keeping your promises.
items.s: If you were high status, then you got what little was available first, but even back then you had to earn your status by taking care of the tribe.

items.c: create a product or a service
items.zh: 创造一种产品或提供一种服务
items.note: product 与 service 的区别，适用于开店和经营。 例：I provide a service that helps clients feel confident.
items.s: Now we have wealth creation where you can actually create a product or a service.

items.note: scale 的商业含义，不只是简单扩大。 例：A useful online course can scale to many students.
items.s: You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.

items.zh: 可供大家争取的地位有限
items.note: go around = 够大家分。 例：There is enough food to go around.
items.s: There’s limited status to go around.

items.note: rise in + 抽象名词；与 fall in status 对照。 例：Her status in the industry rose over time.
items.s: It’s a ranking ladder, it’s a hierarchy, and so if one person rises in status, somebody else has to lower in status.

items.c: whereas wealth creation games can be just you creating products
items.zh: 而创造财富的竞争却可以……
items.note: whereas 对比两种情况。 例：I work with clients, whereas my friend works online.
items.s: They always require direct combat, whereas wealth creation games can be just you creating products – you don’t have to fight anybody else.

items.note: not quite 比 not 更委婉、更精确。 例：Being busy is not quite the same as being productive.
items.s: but that’s not quite the same as invective against other people or being angry with other people or feeling pushed down or pushed up or having a beef with somebody.

items.note: 委婉提出有理由支持的观点，不一定是争吵。 例：I would argue that consistency matters more than speed.
items.s: So I would argue that wealth creation games are both more pleasant, they’re positive-sum, and they actually have concrete material returns.

items.note: trade A for B = 用 A 换 B。 例：Some people trade their free time for a higher salary.
items.s: They want status, so they go to Hollywood, start starring in movies, they donate to non-profits, they go to Cannes or Davos, and they start trying to trade the money for status.

items.note: what 引出名词性内容；不要理解为疑问句。 例：People often want what they cannot easily get.
items.s: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.

items.note: not ... until 关注“到某时才发生”。 例：I didn’t understand it until you explained it.
items.s: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.

items.c: There’s never been an easier time to
items.zh: 从来没有比现在更容易……的时候
items.note: There has never been ... 用现在完成时连接过去到现在的比较。 例：There has never been an easier time to learn online.
items.s: There’s never been an easier time to make money.

items.zh: 外面有这么多可利用的杠杆
items.note: out there 在此指现实世界中存在的机会/工具。 例：There are so many useful tools out there.
items.s: Yes, it’s still hard, but there’s never been an easier time to create wealth, because there’s so much leverage out there, there’s so much opportunity.

items.c: You still have to go find it
items.note: have to 表示必须；go + 动词原形是口语表达。 例：You still have to go find your first customers.
items.s: You still have to go find it, it’s not easy, it’s not gonna fall on your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting,

items.note: be better off doing = 做某事会更有利。 例：You’re better off booking ahead.
items.s: That’s changed, and so I would argue that you’re better off focusing on wealth games than status games.

items.c: get rich off of being famous
items.note: get rich off (of) ... = 靠……获得财富，口语。 例：Some creators get rich off of online content.
items.s: If you’re trying to build up, for example, your following on a social network and get famous and then get rich off of being famous,

items.c: given that most people use status to then try and cash in to achieve wealth
items.zh: 考虑到大多数人利用地位来……
items.note: given that 引出已知前提。 例：Given that it is raining, we should leave early.
items.s: It’s funny how people who have achieved such a level of wealth – you think why do you need the status, given that most people use status to then try and cash in to achieve wealth?

items.zh: 把名望变现来获得财富
items.note: cash in 在上下文指利用名望赚钱；不要理解为存入现金。 例：She built a following and then cashed in.
items.s: It’s funny how people who have achieved such a level of wealth – you think why do you need the status, given that most people use status to then try and cash in to achieve wealth?

items.note: the other direction 指“先财富后地位”的相反路线。 例：We tried one approach and then went in the other direction.
items.s: If you’ve achieved “fuck you money” already, if you’re post-money or asset-heavy as it’s known, why are you trying to go in the other direction?

items.c: win the game and be done with it
items.zh: 赢下这场竞争，然后不再参与
items.note: be done with it = 结束后不再纠缠。 例：I want to finish the project and be done with it.
items.s: Does that mean the reason to play the game is to win the game and be done with it?

items.zh: 我之前还没把这件事想透
items.note: 过去完成时表示在听到对方观点之前尚未充分考虑。 例：I hadn’t thought that through until you asked.
items.s: That’s a good observation, I hadn’t thought that through, but you’re right.

items.c: at a certain level of wealth
items.note: at a certain level = 达到某个不具体的水平。 例：At a certain level, more money matters less.
items.s: I think people will always want more status, but I think you can be satisfied at a certain level of wealth.

items.c: put you in competition against your contemporaries
items.zh: 让你和同时代的同行竞争
items.note: put someone in ... 使某人处于某种状态。 例：Social media puts small businesses in competition with one another.
items.s: but the fact that, for example, iTunes and YouTube can put you in competition against your contemporaries every single day, and make you go up and down and show you likes and comments and ratings.

items.c: keep you running on that treadmill forever
items.zh: 让你永远困在追逐排名的循环里
items.note: keep + someone + V-ing 表示让某人持续做某事。 例：Notifications keep me checking my phone.
items.s: They’ll keep you running on that treadmill forever.

items.c: trajectory is more important than position
items.zh: 发展方向比当前名次更重要
items.note: A is more important than B；trajectory 与 position 对比。 例：Progress is more important than perfection.
items.s: Jimmy Carr has this cool idea where he says trajectory is more important than position.

items.note: unless 引出避免坏结果的条件。 例：The problem will get worse unless we fix it.
items.s: Something that is bleeding eventually dies, unless you stop the bleeding, so you’re hardwired not to lose what you have.

items.c: so close to just not surviving
items.zh: 离活不下去只有一步之遥
items.note: close to + 名词或动名词；not surviving = 没能活下去。 例：They were close to running out of money.
items.s: Because we evolved in conditions where we’re so close to just not surviving, you don’t want to give anything up.

items.note: grip 是动词，tightly 修饰动作。 例：She gripped the handle tightly.
items.s: So you grip tightly?
